subject: Geo inference benchmarks & next steps (hyperscaler comparison)
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudapps.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Geo inference benchmarks & next steps (hyperscaler comparison)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: consistent 95th %-tile latency <= 200ms for short-chat workloads across US/EU regions.
- Main competitor concerns: existing evaluation with hyperscaler endpoints shows variable geo latency and limited regional residency controls.
- Security/procurement: SOC2 + data residency PII handling will be gating for pilot.

Redwood differentiators we discussed
- Multi-region deployment options (hosted + private VPC) with per-region routing and local KV cache to cut geo hops.
- Cost-aware routing: can steer to cheaper model variants for non-critical requests.
- Observability: token-level latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards for correlation with user geography.

Proposed technical next steps (short):
1) We run a small geo benchmark plan (US/EU/APAC) using your sample prompt set (~10k short convo tokens) to capture tail latency and cold-starts.
2) Share preliminary numbers + raw traces (CSV) and an abbreviated bench plan.
3) If results look good, scope a 2-week pilot: dedicated capacity in EU + hosted region in US.

Do we have permission to run those geo tests from our end using the sample prompts you shared? Also, who should we loop in on procurement for any PO/contract discussions (email for CloudApps Procurement would be great).

Attached: redwood-bench-plan-0309.pdf (plan + metrics), prelim-latency-0309.csv (blank template for results).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15m call if helpful.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0146

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudapps.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-09T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo inference benchmarks & next steps (hyperscaler comparison)

Sergio —

Appreciate the clear summary. Yes, please go ahead with the geo tests; a few clarifications before you start: 

1) We ran initial tests against our hyperscaler-based endpoints (AWS and GCP) and saw good US performance but EU tail latency spikes during peak hours. We'll share the CSV of those runs separately.
2) Data residency: EU requests must not leave the EU region. Can Redwood guarantee that for the hosted offering, or would we need Dedicated/Private for that assurance?
3) Procurement: looping in procurement (procurement@cloudapps.io) to align on what a pilot PoC commitment looks like.

Also, are you able to provide an apples-to-apples comparison of request flow between Redwood hosted vs our current hyperscaler endpoints (network hops, who has access to logs, retention defaults)? Those specifics will determine whether legal/procurement will accept the hosted option for the pilot.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudApps Inc.
elena.rossi@cloudapps.io

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudapps.io>, CloudApps Procurement <procurement@cloudapps.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-09T16:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo inference benchmarks & next steps (hyperscaler comparison)

Hi Elena (and procurement team),

Thanks — we'll start the geo benchmark run this afternoon. Short answers to your questions upfront: 

- Data residency: For strict EU-only residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC). Our hosted EU region can provide regionally isolated serving and data-at-rest encryption, but Dedicated/Private provides contractual residency and KMS control. We'll call this out clearly in the pilot options.

- Apples-to-apples flow: attached bench plan includes a simplified flowchart (client -> regional ingress -> model service -> KV cache -> response) and notes on log access/retention. In short: on hosted, logs are available in the Console per-tenant with default 30d retention (configurable with add-ons); on Dedicated/Private customers control retention and KMS.

Prelim numbers (short-chat, p50/p95) from our internal dry-run (do not treat as final):
- US (us-west1): p50 42ms, p95 118ms
- EU (europe-west2): p50 58ms, p95 240ms (noting cold-starts at peak)
- APAC (asia-east1): p50 76ms, p95 290ms

We will run the tests using your prompt set and push raw traces + CSV to the Drive link when done. Expected ETA for raw results: 24 hours. We'll also include a comparison sheet mapping which hyperscaler metrics (eg. ELB latency, model-serving time) align to our Console traces.

Next asks: 
- Please confirm permission to run the tests on your sample prompts and confirm the procurement contact on your side for a pilot PO.
- Any blackout windows we should avoid for EU region testing?

Attaching: redwood-bench-plan-0309.pdf (detailed steps), prelim-latency-0309.csv (pre-populated with internal dry-run rows).

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0146

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Geo inference benchmarks & next steps (hyperscaler comparison)

Elena / Procurement —

Following up from Sergio's notes. Quick commercial and pilot logistics: 

Pilot options (summary)
- Hosted pilot (US + EU region): 30-day usage budget, standard hosted T&Cs, 30d logs. Good for validating latency/behavior quickly.
- Dedicated pilot (reserved pool in EU + hosted US): 2-week reserved capacity trial with SLA and KMS control; recommended if CloudApps requires contractual data residency.

Commercial asks: 
- Pilot PO: typically $10k commitment credited against first-month consumption for Dedicated; hosted pilots often go by usage. Procurement, please advise which route you'd prefer so we can pull a tailored SOW.

Technical follow-up: Sergio will drop the full bench results to the Drive link and we can schedule a 30m readout the day after the results land (propose Thu 2026-03-12 10:00 PT / 18:00 CET — let us know what works).

Markus + I are available to join the readout to cover deployment options and contractual language.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
